summary: Phase 3C BLOCKED: same_side proved mathematically false for unsorted selections. GHR93 assumes sorted a_0 < ... < a_n; resolution requires restructuring ghr93_case_II with sorting preprocessing + U(B,A) witness (~500-800 lines).

blocking_issues.issue: same_side lemma is mathematically FALSE for unsorted selections. 8+ approaches tried, all fail. Root cause: rank-r formula agreement does not determine ordering relative to a third point. GHR93 proof requires sorted selections.
blocking_issues.root_cause: Counterexample: let a_init(k) = extendPoint p_n (same point selected twice) and a'_big(k) be any point with same depth-r type at a different linear order position. Then a'_big(k) < p_n is possible while a_init(k) = p_n. Biconditional fails.
blocking_issues.resolution: Restructure ghr93_case_II: (1) Add sorting preprocessing using Tuple.sort (already imported). (2) Generalize proof so point can be at arbitrary position, not just position n. (3) With sorted selections, all a_init(k) < p_n, making sel_pn_ord trivial. (4) Use ghr93_winning_condition_perm to permute result. Complication: in extended carrier, gaps above p_n mean p_n may not be the maximum element; must handle gaps specially.

continuation_context.key_finding: same_side IS MATHEMATICALLY FALSE. Two points with the same depth-r type CAN be on opposite sides of a third point. This is not a proof engineering issue; it is a fundamental mathematical impossibility. The ONLY resolution is the GHR93 approach: sort selections so all a_init(k) < p_n, then sel_pn_ord holds trivially.

resolution_plan.option_c: Verify if elements above p_n are always gaps (would simplify greatly). If yes, gap ordering has special properties that might bypass same_side.
